comparison: Both evaluate scRNA-seq cell clustering claims (C33-C37). OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED despite acknowledging n=1 per genotype limitation. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, emphasizing 'too few cells to support firm conclusions' and 'lack of replicates' making differences unreliable.

Both assess cell-type specific laminin expression claims (C38-C42). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with acknowledgment of limited samples. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to 'low number of cells analyzed and lack of replicates' and note findings are 'purely correlative' without functional validation.

Both evaluate bulk RNA-seq claims (C52-C54). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate sample sizes and statistical analyses. Peer reviewers acknowledge 'substantial' samples making data 'potentially more robust' and a 'valuable resource,' though note data are correlative.

Both assess integrin pathway claims (C61-C65). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED but notes mechanistic inference (C65) is somewhat speculative. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, emphasizing 'all data are correlative and do not provide functional insights' for the integrin-mediated damage mechanism.

Both evaluate overall model validity claim (C93). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on comprehensive characterization. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting the model 'lacks significant insights' beyond existing LAMA2-MD models and questioning added value despite technical validity.

Both address phenotypic characterization claims (C12-C20 in OpenEval; C12-C22 in peer review). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval acknowledges grip strength measurement limitations. Peer reviewers note phenotype 'is fully consistent with the data from others' and replicates previous models.

Both evaluate myelin-related gene expression claims (C49-C50). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting statistical significance and biological relevance. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, emphasizing 'all data are correlative and do not provide functional insights' and connection to human disease remains speculative.

Both assess histological pathology claims (C23-C25, C67-C68 in OpenEval; broader set including C27-C30 in peer review). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes temporal progression documentation. Peer reviewers acknowledge findings are 'fully consistent with the data from others.'

Both evaluate mouse model creation claims (C10-C11). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes detailed methodological validation. Peer reviewers acknowledge the work 'adds another mouse model' and confirm 'phenotype is fully consistent' with previous models without methodological concerns.

Both assess cytoskeleton protein expression claims (C55-C57 in OpenEval; C55-C60 in peer review). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate sample sizes and regional heterogeneity. Peer reviewers consider these part of 'potentially more robust' bulk RNA-seq resource as descriptive characterization.

Both evaluate comparative claims about model similarity to human disease (C69, C71-C72). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes consistency between MRI and histology but acknowledges C71 is somewhat speculative. Peer reviewers accept phenotype is 'fully consistent with the data from others.'

Both assess ECM upregulation and fibrosis claims (C82-C83). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes histological evidence supports inference though causality is inferred. Peer reviewers accept as part of 'valuable resource' bulk RNA-seq data, though mechanistic interpretation remains correlative.

Overlapping evaluation of regeneration-related protein claims (C58-C60). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED (R15 includes C58-C60, C80) noting regional heterogeneity explains discrepancies. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED (R9 includes C55-C60) as part of descriptive characterization resource.

Both address BBB-related pathway claims (C43-C45 in OpenEval; broader BBB claims C43-C51, C89-C90 in peer review). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for GO/CellChat analysis. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED for BBB conclusions, stating findings are 'purely correlative' and require experimental validation like dye leakage tests.

Both evaluate cell-cell communication and compensatory mechanism claims (C46-C48 in OpenEval; part of broader BBB evaluation in peer review). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED though notes compensatory inference needs validation. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED for BBB-related conclusions due to lack of functional validation.

Partial overlap on laminin α2 loss and collagen VI compensation (C26-C28 in OpenEval; C27-C28 in peer review R3). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes Western blot and immunofluorescence validation. Peer reviewers accept as part of phenotype consistent with other models.

Partial overlap on muscle-type specificity claims (C29-C30, C70 in OpenEval; C29-C30 in peer review R3). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes selective sparing of cardiac/smooth muscle is important observation. Peer reviewers accept as part of replicated phenotype.

Partial overlap on regeneration interpretation (C80 in OpenEval R15; C78, C80 in peer review R13). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED but notes speculation. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, emphasizing data are 'correlative' and recommend authors 'temper their interpretations.'

Partial overlap on model comparison claim (C66 in both). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes similarity to human disease validates model relevance though comparison is qualitative. Peer reviewers acknowledge model 'reiterates the phenotype of previously published models.'

Partial overlap on human disease similarity (C72 in both). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes qualitative comparison with human literature. Peer reviewers accept phenotype is 'fully consistent with the data from others.'

Partial overlap on MRI findings (C21-C22 in OpenEval R4; included in broader phenotype C12-C22 in peer review R2). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes statistical significance and consistency with histology. Peer reviewers accept as part of replicated phenotype.

Minimal overlap on laminin α2 loss (C26 in both). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes Western blot validation. Peer reviewers accept as part of basic model characterization without methodological concerns.

Minimal overlap on muscle pathology (C70 in both). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes tissue-specific expression pattern. Peer reviewers accept as comparative observation consistent with other models.

Minimal overlap on contractile impairment speculation (C78 in both). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting C78 is explicitly speculative but reasonable. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, emphasizing correlative nature and recommending tempered interpretations.

Minimal overlap on brain/BBB claims (C89-C90 in both). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, acknowledging absence of direct MRI evidence for cortical malformations. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED for BBB conclusions, requiring experimental validation beyond correlative molecular findings.

Minimal overlap on BBB disruption inference (C51 in both). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED though notes direct permeability measurements would strengthen evidence. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, explicitly stating BBB conclusion 'remains purely correlative' and requires functional validation.
